niche.habitat: Periphery of cryo-jet plumes and tidal flexure fissures
niche.diet: H2 flux, precipitating silanes, microbial mats

body: Rigid arachnoid crystal frame; joints filled with supercooled CH4/Ethane slush that flows only near 115 K

links: Low thermal energy restricts molecular motion

skill.effect: The creature lunges forward to strike, shattering its target with brittle force before instantly freezing itself solid and remaining motionless.

chains.weakness: Shatters if cooled mid-strike; cannot move during inter-pulse periods.

journal.en: It waits as a statue for a heartbeat of warmth, then strikes like lightning.

plausibility.summary: At 60–110 K equilibrium (F2), siloxane and mineralized silicate matrices stay glassy and stiff; low thermal energy limits segmental flexion (F14). Weaker gravity (F4) relaxes scaling limits on a hollow arachnoid frame so a large brittle exoskeleton is structurally affordable without the crushing weight penalty familiar from terrestrial giants. Explosive engage-then-stillness fits a pulse-fed ectotherm: almost no ATP turnover between cryo-jet events (F15), then brief local warming for one strike. Predation by shattering Sifon-Hielo’s open lattice is mechanically consistent with a rigid impactor versus a porous sessile filterer.

links: Supercooled solvent slush melts at 115 K

skill.effect: It dashes forward at a blistering pace for a short while, then quickly refreezes and stands completely still, unable to act afterward.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to wind and vibration during thaw; movement causes structural stress.

journal.en: Its limbs liquefy into liquid glass for a brief, terrifying dance.

skill.effect: Its crystalline body swells and hardens as it absorbs energy, growing noticeably tougher and more aggressive as it blooms.

chains.weakness: Growth consumes stored chemical reserves; weakens after pulse.

journal.en: In the warmth, it grows as much in an hour as it would in a year.

plausibility.summary: Baseline turnover at ~80 K is days–weeks (F15); a pulse that raises tissue microsites toward ~110–120 K can accelerate silane/organosilicon deposition and metal-catalyzed redox (F13, F15) by many orders of magnitude in Arrhenius terms, so ‘an hour ≈ a year’ is acceptable as documentary hyperbole if reserves are finite. Post-pulse weakening from drained storage is mandatory honest budgeting on a world where silane chemistry only runs when cryo solvents stay anhydrous and reducing (F8, F17) — HF-style recycling (F13) is highly speculative but keeps the causal chain closed.

links: Cold dense air favors low-frequency sound

skill.effect: It tilts its head and scans the area, causing faint heat shimmer to outline any nearby living creatures.

journal.en: It navigates the blind fog by listening to the world's heat and song.

plausibility.summary: Perpetual methane frost fog (F10) kills usable vision; dense N2–CH4 air favors low-frequency sound propagation over highs (F9), so infrasonic gradient tracking plus IR pits (F18) is the expected sensory stack for a jet-zone predator. Passive thermal sense out to ~15 m matches pit-organ physics (ΔT, not long-range vision). Diet on H2 flux and precipitating silanes aligns with reducing atmosphere and vent redox (F8, F15).
